title: Vegetation Greening Modulates Precipitation Pattern in China: Enhanced Moisture Recycling and Increased Atmospheric Instabilities Driven by Land‐Atmosphere Feedbacks
content:
Abstract

The land use and land cover change (LUCC) is disrupting the water and energy balances of the land surface recently, thereby modulating precipitation formation through land-atmosphere feedbacks. However, this effect has not been fully quantified across the nine major river basins in China with distinct natural conditions. In this study, the local and remote effects of the LUCC on precipitation were evaluated using an advanced moisture tracking model. The results reveal that the greening trend of vegetation has enhanced land-atmosphere feedbacks since 1999, which was mainly reflected by increasing evapotranspiration (ET). This feedback mechanism led to an increasing recycling ratio of precipitation (0.003–0.009 decade−1), precipitable water vapor (0.30–1.28 mm/decade) and a general decrease in the lifting condensation level (−181.8 to 43.3 m/decade). Increasing atmospheric moisture also induced a rise (0.1%–9.9%) in the proportion of days with high convective available potential energy values, indicating an increase in atmospheric instabilities associated with increased atmospheric convection and precipitation. Increasing ET moisture from the Three-North Region increased precipitation in the North China Plain and Northeast China Plain by 4.7–75.1 mm/decade through remote effect, while its contribution to the local and downwind extreme precipitation remained stable under the LUCC. Afforestation in the Yellow River and Inland River Basins has reached the sustainability threshold, while it remains sustainable in other river basins in China. This study will provide a solid scientific basis for supporting the optimization of ecological engineering planning in different basins with diverse climatic and land cover conditions.
